data.name: Isle of Man
data.summary: Self-governing Crown Dependency outside the UK and EU. No capital gains tax, no inheritance or gift tax, no wealth tax. Income, including dividends, is taxed at 10%/21%; residents can fix their total income tax at £220,000 a year (£440,000 per couple) for 5 or 10 years.

regimes.name: Ordinary Isle of Man residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals pay income tax at 10% and 21% on worldwide income. No capital gains, inheritance, gift or wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence in the Isle of Man (see residency test). Living there requires a right of abode / immigration permission for non-British, non-Irish nationals.

capital_gains.summary: The Isle of Man has no capital gains tax. Gains by a resident private investor on listed shares, bonds, a private business or real estate are not taxed. Gains that amount to trading (frequent dealing, property development) are taxed as income at up to 21%.

open_questions: The PwC 'other taxes' page does not state 'no CGT' in terms; confirm with the Income Tax Division's own statement if precision on land-development profits is needed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax exists. PwC lists income tax as the only tax on income ('There are no other taxes on income'); capital gains are outside the income tax charge unless they are trading profits.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Profits from a trade in shares or land (badges of trade: frequency, financing, intention) are income taxed at 10%/21%. A buy-and-hold family portfolio is not normally a trade.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed as ordinary income: 10% on the first £6,500 of taxable income (single), 21% above. A large dividend income is therefore taxed at 21% (personal allowance £17,000 is withdrawn above £100,000). Residents can elect a tax cap of £220,000 a year (see special regime).
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Personal allowance £17,000 single / £34,000 jointly assessed, reduced by £1 per £2 of income above £100,000 / £200,000. 10% band £6,500 / £13,000.

open_questions: Credit relief mechanics (unilateral relief for non-treaty source countries) and exact treaty count not verified from an official list.
dividends.rate_basis: Top marginal income tax rate 21% for 2026/27 (gov.im rates table). Manx companies are mostly taxed at 0%, so there is no imputation credit on domestic dividends. Foreign tax relief with no agreement: restricted to the lower of the overseas tax suffered and the Manx income tax due on the income, if reasonable steps were taken to minimise the overseas tax (Income Tax Division); so a 15% withholding is credited in full against 21%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends paid by Isle of Man companies (PwC).
dividends.treaty_network: Small network of double tax agreements (UK, Guernsey, Jersey and a handful of others); no income tax treaty with the United States, so US-source dividends suffer 30% US withholding. Relief for foreign withholding tax is by credit against Manx tax.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the 'holding_company' structure regime: a Manx company pays 0% on investment income and gains; distributions to a resident shareholder are income taxed at 21%; the attribution regime that taxed undistributed profits was abolished (accounting periods after 6 April 2012).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local rates (property tax) are charged on occupied property; amounts are modest and not a wealth tax.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax, estate duty or gift tax. Only a court probate fee on Isle of Man assets is payable, capped at £9,422.50 for estates over £1 million (2024 schedule).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Probate court fee on the gross value of Isle of Man estate only: £31.50 up to £10,000 rising to a flat £9,422.50 above £1,000,000 (fees as at 2024). Negligible relative to a large estate, hence 0.

inheritance.domicile_rules: No domicile or residence test applies because there is no tax. A family arriving from the UK should check the UK's residence-based inheritance tax (from 6 April 2025: long-term UK residents remain within UK IHT for up to 10 years after leaving).

regimes.name: Income tax cap election
regimes.description: A resident individual may elect to cap total Isle of Man income tax at £220,000 a year (£440,000 for a jointly assessed couple) for 2026/27 elections. The cap amount in the first year applies for the whole 5- or 10-year election period, and it is payable each year even if normal tax would have been lower.
regimes.eligibility: Must be, or be about to become, Isle of Man tax resident. Election in writing with details of wealth and income, approved by the Assessor; new residents must elect within 60 days of starting residence. Fixed period of 5 or 10 consecutive tax years, renewable.
regimes.duration_note: Each election fixes the cap for 5 or 10 consecutive tax years (Income Tax Division guidance note GN51) and can be renewed by a further election, with no limit on renewals, so the cap is available for as long as the person stays resident. It ends if the person leaves or does not renew; the cap amount is fixed at the first-year figure for each election period.

lump_sum.notes: £220,000 single / £440,000 jointly assessed couple (2026/27). Payable each year of the 5- or 10-year election regardless of actual income (GN51 s3.2). Capital gains are untaxed anyway. Renewable, so treated as indefinite. Elected by the individual who holds the income: spouses are taxed independently by default (joint taxation is an option), so a couple with the portfolio in one name pays one cap (GBP 220,000) and a jointly assessed couple pays GBP 440,000. Not indexed: the amount is fixed per election period at the first-year figure and changes only by Budget. Where an unforeseen fall in income would make the cap dearer than normal assessment, the Assessor will permit taxation on the normal basis (GN51 s.8.1); for a family with stable high income the cap is a fixed charge.

dividends.summary: Under the cap, the whole income tax bill is fixed at £220,000 (single) or £440,000 (couple) a year, so additional dividends carry no extra Manx tax once ordinary tax at 21% would exceed the cap (roughly £1.05m of taxable income for a single person).

regimes.name: Manx investment holding company (0% company)
regimes.description: The family funds a Manx company that holds the listed portfolio. Manx companies pay 0% income tax on investment income, and there is no capital gains tax, so the company pays nothing on dividends or gains. A distribution to a resident shareholder is income taxed at 10%/21%. Profits kept in the company are not taxed on the shareholder: the distributable profits charge (repealed for periods from 6 April 2008) and the attribution regime that replaced it (abolished for accounting periods after 6 April 2012) no longer apply. Foreign withholding tax on the company's dividends is a final cost.
regimes.eligibility: Any Isle of Man resident can incorporate a company in the Isle of Man; a resident company pays the standard 0% rate. It must be a passive investment holder: banking and large retail profits are taxed at 10% and Manx land and property income at 20%. US citizens are excluded (CFC/PFIC rules).
regimes.duration_note: Ordinary company rules with no time limit; the company lasts as long as the family keeps it.

structure.entity: Private company limited by shares (Companies Act 2006, Isle of Man), investment holding
structure.payout_notes: Dividends from a Manx company to a resident individual are income taxed at the top rate of 21% in 2026/27 (the 10% band covers only the first GBP 6,500; the personal allowance is withdrawn above GBP 100,000). Profits kept in the company are not taxed on the shareholder (Distributable Profits Charge repealed for periods from 6 April 2008; Attribution Regime for Individuals abolished for accounting periods after 6 April 2012; Income Tax Division).
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: The attribution regime for individuals was abolished, so no look-through applies to undistributed profits; other anti-avoidance in the Income Tax Act 1970 and any substance or filing rules for a passive holding company were not reviewed. The Companies Act 2006 requirements and their cost are not sourced here.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Treatment of liquidation distributions to a resident shareholder not researched. The shares of a Manx company are Manx assets, so probate on a death is charged on them at the Manx court fee (GBP 9,422.50 above GBP 1,000,000, as at November 2024), whereas foreign shares held directly pay none; the model carries no fixed fee.

assumptions: The family arrives as new residents; the top rate of 21% applies to dividends of about GBP 520,000 a year (the personal allowance is withdrawn above GBP 100,000 and the 10% band is only GBP 6,500). Allowances are ignored.

Foreign dividends carry a 15% withholding from a country without a Manx treaty; relief is the lower of the foreign tax and the Manx tax on the income, so the 15% is credited in full against 21% (the Division requires reasonable steps to minimise the overseas tax).

Spouses are taxed independently by default, with joint taxation an option. The portfolio is assumed to be in one spouse's name, so one cap of GBP 220,000 applies (GBP 440,000 only for a jointly assessed couple, or if both spouses elected). The cap is fixed per election period and changed only by Budget (GBP 200,000 until 2024/25, GBP 220,000 since 2025/26), so it is not indexed.

The holding company is funded with cash or shares at today's value and pays distributions equal to the family's spending, taxed at 21% in the shareholders' hands (dividends are income). The estate probate fee on the company's shares, a fixed GBP 9,422.50 above GBP 1,000,000 of Manx estate, is not modelled; it is under 0.1% of GBP 10m.
The inheritance check is for foreign listed shares held directly; the Manx probate fee falls only on Manx assets.
open_questions: Tax cap and ordinary tax: the cap is payable even when ordinary tax is lower; the Assessor will let a taxpayer be taxed on the normal basis during an election only if income projections proved over-optimistic through unforeseen change (GN51 s.8.1). The model charges the fixed cap for as long as the family stays.

Needs an engine change: after the 5- or 10-year election ends the family may renew or revert to ordinary tax, and may re-elect only 'before the start of the first tax year' of a period; the model keeps the cap for 60 years. The choice between the cap and ordinary tax each period (whichever is cheaper over the next 5 or 10 years, with a cap fixed at the first-year amount) cannot be expressed.
Lifetime gifts attract no tax (tax file), so a family would pass assets to children while alive; the engine has taxable events only at the two deaths.
Manx trusts and foundations were considered but not added: they save no income tax for a resident family and their treatment and running costs were not sourced.
Holding company: annual running cost not sourced and the tax file records none; the check counts none. Treatment of liquidation distributions to a resident shareholder was not researched.
The probate fee order was read through a law-firm guide (November 2024), not the Order itself.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: Income tax at 10% on the first GBP 6,500 and 21% above on worldwide dividends, with credit for foreign withholding tax; no capital gains, wealth or inheritance tax. The probate court fee falls only on Manx assets, so a foreign portfolio pays none.

paths.name: Income tax cap election (GBP 220,000 a year)
paths.note: The individual elects, within 60 days of becoming resident, to pay a fixed GBP 220,000 a year for 5 or 10 tax years, renewable (GN51). It is payable each year even if ordinary tax would be lower, and for this family ordinary tax is about GBP 109,000, so the cap costs more; it pays only above about GBP 1.05m of taxable income. The portfolio is assumed to be in one spouse's name, so one cap applies.

paths.name: Manx investment holding company
paths.note: A Manx company owns the portfolio and pays 0% tax on dividends and gains; the resident shareholders pay income tax at 21% on dividends they receive, and profits kept in the company are not taxed on them. The estate holds the shares, which are Manx assets, so probate would attract the Manx court fee (not modelled).

immigration.name: Isle of Man
immigration.summary: The Isle of Man is not in the EU and has had no EU free movement since 31 December 2020. British and Irish citizens may live here freely under the Common Travel Area (they still need a work permit to work unless exempt or an 'Isle of Man worker'). Everyone else, EU and US citizens included, needs a visa. There is no investor, retirement or digital nomad visa (Tier 1 Investor is closed). The open routes are the Start-up visa (no investment threshold, 2 years 4 months, no settlement), the Innovator visa (at least GBP 50,000 of investment funds, endorsed by the Department for Enterprise, settlement after 3 years) and the Worker Migrant visa (an Island employer, salary at least GBP 25,447.50).
immigration.naturalisation: British citizenship under the British Nationality Act 1981, applied for through the Isle of Man Nationality Service, normally after settlement (indefinite leave to remain); naturalisation fee GBP 1,858.20 (gov.im, accessed 17 October 2026). The usual UK residence period (5 years, with ILR held 12 months) was not stated on the gov.im page read. Irish citizens have a simplified route since 24 September 2025.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Not verified from a fetched source.

routes.name: Common Travel Area (British and Irish citizens)
routes.summary: British and Irish citizens can move to the Isle of Man and live here without immigration permission. Only these two nationalities benefit; other EU and other-passport holders do not.
routes.requirements: Per the Department for Enterprise guide, 'only British and Irish passport holders are normally free to move to the Isle of Man and take up residence without the need for Immigration permission'. Irish citizens (EU group) and British citizens (OTHER group) only. Employment still needs an Isle of Man work permit under the Control of Employment Act 2014 unless the person is an 'Isle of Man worker' or the job is exempt (per the March 2026 immigration notice, Irish citizens need a work permit unless exempt).
routes.fees_note: No immigration fee. Work permit application: GBP 60 paid by the employer (gov.im page last updated 31 October 2017; the June 2024 guide repeats GBP 60).
routes.tax_note: A visa does not by itself decide Isle of Man tax residence.

routes.summary: For first-time founders with an innovative, viable and scalable business idea endorsed by the Department for Enterprise. No investment threshold; leave is 2 years 4 months and cannot lead to settlement, but holders may switch to Innovator.

routes.summary: For experienced business people who set up, join or take over a business on the Island with at least GBP 50,000 of investment funds, endorsed by the Department for Enterprise. Leave is 3 years at a time, with settlement possible after 3 years.

routes.name: Worker Migrant visa (Appendix W) and work permit
routes.limited_places: Needs an employer who passes the labour market test; the Department decides each case (no right to a permit)
routes.summary: A job offer from an Isle of Man employer in an eligible occupation, with a Confirmation of Employment from the Immigration Service. Salary must be at least GBP 25,447.50 a year or the occupation rate, and the employer must first test the local market.
routes.requirements: Appendix W: valid Confirmation of Employment (CoE) in an eligible occupation (Appendix Skilled Occupations or Shortage Occupation List); salary at least the higher of GBP 25,447.50 a year or the occupation rate (for new applicants from 31 October 2025; new Worker Migrant rules from 1 June 2026); English language; maintenance funds under Appendix C (employer may instead undertake to maintain, GBP 1,270 a month for 3 months); the vacancy must not be fillable by a settled worker (Sequential Labour Market Test, unless exempt). No self-employment. Under the Control of Employment Act 2014 a work permit is also needed unless the holder has an 'immigration employment document' (a visa of this kind) or the job is exempt. ILR after 5 years' continuous residence (absences up to 180 days in a year) with employer confirmation of salary and English plus Life in the UK knowledge.
routes.fees_note: Entry clearance fee not listed on gov.im ('see form for fees'); CoE for entry clearance: no charge; SET W (ILR): GBP 3,226; work permit GBP 60 (employer).
routes.physical_presence: Live and work on the Island; no more than 180 days absent in a year for settlement
routes.family: Partner and children can apply as dependants (Part 8 / Appendix FM). Partners of permit holders get an automatic 1-year work permit.
routes.tax_note: A visa does not by itself decide Isle of Man tax residence.

routes.name: EU Settlement Scheme (Appendix EU)
routes.status_note: Free movement ended on 31 December 2020. The scheme was for people resident before 1 January 2021; its application deadline (30 June 2021 per gov.im) has passed. Not a route for someone arriving today.
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens who lived on the Island before 2021 could apply for status. New arrivals from the EU need a visa like anyone else.
routes.requirements: Residence in the Isle of Man before 1 January 2021. Closed to new arrivals; the Island's scheme is aligned with the UK EUSS under Appendix EU. No charge.
routes.physical_presence: Continuous residence rules apply; not checked in detail

open_questions: Entry clearance fees for Start-up, Innovator, Worker Migrant and Ancestry are paid to UK Visas and Immigration and were not found on gov.im; government_fees is null for those routes. Known in-country fees: FLR Start Up GBP 666, FLR Innovator GBP 1,693, SET GBP 3,226; endorsement GBP 1,000.

A law firm reports some Isle of Man immigration fees rise from 1 August 2026 to match the UK; the gov.im fee table read on 17 October 2026 shows the figures quoted here, but the effective date was not confirmed.
Years to British citizenship per route (ordinary 5 years of residence with ILR held 12 months) not confirmed on a gov.im page; path_to_citizenship_years left null.
Dual citizenship not verified from an official source.
No retiree, financially independent person or digital nomad route found in the Immigration Rules (confirmed only by absence from the Appendices and gov.im pages read).

A 2023 Department for Enterprise news item proposed temporarily suspending work permits (replacing them with employer registration); the June 2024 guide and a March 2026 notice show the work permit system still operating. Current status of any suspension not confirmed.

Worker Migrant: the current Appendix Skilled Occupations / Shortage Occupation List salary rates and the Sequential Labour Market Test details were not read in full; GBP 25,447.50 is the general floor.
Ancestry route: absence limits, fees and processing times not checked.
Maintenance funds for Worker Migrant under Appendix C (beyond the GBP 1,270 a month employer undertaking) not read.
Whether the Common Travel Area route should list Irish citizens under the EU group (used here with British citizens under OTHER, only_some_nationalities true).
